doc.title: Jon-Erik Kellso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Career goals
summary: He hopes for more albums as leader, playing with heroes, finding his own voice, and a little more money.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Well if we were to do an interview every ten years, do you have any career goals in mind that ten years from now we’d be talking about the fact that you have done what?

Well I’m pretty happy with the way things are going. I’ve already gotten to do two albums of my own and I’ve played with some of my heroes. It’s not that I’ve done it all yet, I don’t mean that, but I’d like to continue to do more work as a leader perhaps and do more albums as a leader as well as playing with more of my heroes and just making great music, the greatest music I can, and trying to put music out there that people want to hear and maybe come up more and more with some of my own ideas and ways of playing it that increasingly have my own voice basically. And I wouldn’t mind making a little bit of money along the way too. I know people don’t like to think about musicians thinking about that but I wouldn’t mind having a little bit more money in the bank.
Don’t you just do it for the love of it?
Well mostly, yeah. Or else I would have maybe been a stockbroker or something, if I was really concerned about making money.
